austronesian-peoples.name: Austronesian peoples
austronesian-peoples.summary: Peoples descended from a prehistoric seaborne migration out of Taiwan around 3000–1500 BCE, who used sails and outrigger boats to spread across the Indo-Pacific, from Madagascar to Easter Island and New Zealand.

khok-phanom-di.name: Khok Phanom Di
khok-phanom-di.summary: A prehistoric mound settlement in Thailand occupied roughly 2000 to 1500 BCE, built up from shell middens and pottery waste beside a rich mangrove estuary, notable for its well-preserved cemetery including a richly furnished 'Princess' burial.

bang-pakong-river.name: Bang Pakong River
bang-pakong-river.summary: A river in eastern Thailand flowing 231 kilometres from near Kabin Buri into the Gulf of Thailand, home to endangered Irrawaddy dolphins and a rare endemic sheatfish species.

ban-non-wat.name: Ban Non Wat
ban-non-wat.summary: A village in Nakhon Ratchasima Province, Thailand, excavated since 2002, revealing 11 prehistoric phases and 640 burials spanning the Neolithic, Bronze and Iron Ages.

mun-river.name: Mun River
mun-river.summary: A tributary of the Mekong River in Thailand that carries about 26 cubic kilometres of water each year.

nakhon-ratchasima-province.name: Nakhon Ratchasima province
nakhon-ratchasima-province.summary: A province in northeastern Thailand (Isan), the country's second-largest by area, whose capital city is also called Khorat.

ban-chiang.name: Ban Chiang
ban-chiang.summary: An archaeological site in Udon Thani province, Thailand, and UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1992, known for ancient red-painted pottery and evidence of early agriculture and metalworking.

udon-thani-province.name: Udon Thani province
udon-thani-province.summary: A province of about 11,072 km² in upper northeastern Thailand (Isan), whose capital city shares its name.

northern-mariana-islands.name: Northern Mariana Islands
northern-mariana-islands.summary: U.S. commonwealth made up of the 14 northern islands of the Mariana Archipelago in the Pacific; ruled successively by Spain, Germany and Japan before joining the United States as a territory in 1986.

chamorro-people.name: Chamorro people
chamorro-people.summary: The Indigenous people of the Mariana Islands, today divided between Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands, with tens of thousands more living across the United States.

ph-ng-nguy-n-culture.name: Phùng Nguyên culture
ph-ng-nguy-n-culture.summary: A Bronze Age culture of Vietnam dated to about 2,000 to 1,500 BC, named for a site east of Việt Trì, known for rice cultivation and polished stone tools.

m-n-b-c.name: Mán Bạc
m-n-b-c.summary: A Neolithic archaeological site in northern Vietnam dated to around 1,850–1,650 BC, the largest known burial site of the Phùng Nguyên culture, with 95 graves.

vi-t-tr.name: Việt Trì
vi-t-tr.summary: Former city in northeastern Vietnam (population 260,288 in 2010) and former capital of Phú Thọ Province, traditionally regarded as the first capital of Vietnam; it ceased to exist as a municipal city in 2025.

guangxi.name: Guangxi
guangxi.summary: An autonomous region in South China bordering Vietnam, home to the largest ethnic minority population in China, chiefly the Zhuang people.

guangdong.name: Guangdong
guangdong.summary: A coastal province in South China, home to Guangzhou and Shenzhen, historically the starting point of the ancient Maritime Silk Road.

shang-dynasty.name: Shang dynasty
shang-dynasty.summary: A Chinese royal dynasty that ruled the Yellow River valley in the 2nd millennium BCE, the earliest Chinese dynasty confirmed by archaeology, known for oracle-bone writing found at its capital near Anyang.

l-c-long-qu-n.name: Lạc Long Quân
l-c-long-qu-n.summary: Legendary king of Vietnam's Hồng Bàng dynasty; with his wife Âu Cơ he is said to be the mythical ancestor of the Vietnamese people.

u-c.name: Âu Cơ
u-c.summary: In Vietnamese creation myth, an immortal mountain snow goddess who married Lạc Long Quân and bore a hundred children regarded as ancestors of the Vietnamese people.

i-vi-t-s-k-to-n-th.name: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư
i-vi-t-s-k-to-n-th.summary: The official national chronicle of Đại Việt, compiled by royal historian Ngô Sĩ Liên and finished in 1479. Its fifteen volumes cover history from the legendary Hồng Bàng dynasty to 1428 and remain a key historical source.
i-vi-t-s-k-to-n-th.source_title: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư

kinh-d-ng-v-ng.name: Kinh Dương Vương
kinh-d-ng-v-ng.summary: A legendary king credited as the first sovereign of the Vietnamese people and founder of the Hồng Bàng dynasty, said in a 15th-century chronicle to have ruled the state of Xích Quỷ from 2879 BC.

h-ng-b-ng-dynasty.name: Hồng Bàng period
h-ng-b-ng-dynasty.summary: Legendary ancient period in Vietnamese history, said in a 15th-century chronicle to have begun in 2879 BC when Kinh Dương Vương founded the kingdom of Xích Quỷ, later renamed Văn Lang.

phong-ch-u.name: Phong Châu
phong-ch-u.summary: Capital city of the ancient kingdom of Văn Lang (now Vietnam) for most of the Hồng Bàng period, from the Third to the eighteenth dynasty of Hùng kings.

ph-th-province.name: Phú Thọ
ph-th-province.summary: A province in northern Vietnam near Hanoi, associated with the presence of ancient Vietnamese people and known for numerous archaeological finds including ancient bronze drums.

l-nh-nam-ch-ch-qu-i.name: Lĩnh Nam chích quái
l-nh-nam-ch-ch-qu-i.summary: 14th-century Vietnamese collection of folklore tales written in chữ Hán by Trần Thế Pháp, later reworked by other editors.

b-nh-ch-ng.name: Bánh chưng
b-nh-ch-ng.summary: A traditional Vietnamese cake of glutinous rice, mung beans and pork, said to have been invented by Prince Lang Liêu and central to Tết celebrations.

b-nh-gi-y.name: Bánh giầy
b-nh-gi-y.summary: A white, round Vietnamese glutinous rice cake, often served with sausage and traditionally paired with bánh chưng as a symbol of the sky.

ng-s-li-n.name: Ngô Sĩ Liên
ng-s-li-n.summary: Vietnamese historian of the Lê dynasty.

shennong.name: Shennong
shennong.summary: A mythological Chinese ruler and deity credited with teaching agriculture and herbal medicine, counted among the legendary Three Sovereigns of prehistoric China.

isan.name: Isan
isan.summary: Region of northeastern Thailand on the Khorat Plateau, the country's largest region, whose population is predominantly ethnic Lao.

batanes.name: Batanes Islands
batanes.summary: The northernmost and smallest province of the Philippines, an island group about 162 km north of Luzon and 190 km south of Taiwan, with its capital at Basco.

melanesia.name: Melanesia
melanesia.summary: A subregion of Oceania in the southwestern Pacific, stretching from New Guinea to Fiji, home to a diverse mix of peoples, languages, and cultures.

red-river-delta.name: Red River Delta
red-river-delta.summary: The low-lying plain formed by the Red River in northern Vietnam, densely populated and devoted mainly to rice farming, considered the cradle of the Vietnamese nation.

austroasiatic-languages.name: Austroasiatic languages
austroasiatic-languages.summary: A family of about 168 languages spoken across Mainland Southeast Asia, South Asia and southern China, including Vietnamese and Khmer, the only two used as national languages.

an-d-ng-v-ng.name: An Dương Vương
an-d-ng-v-ng.summary: Founding and only king of the Âu Lạc kingdom in Vietnam's Red River Delta, who united the Âu Việt and Lạc Việt peoples and died by suicide after his defeat by Nanyue forces in 179 BCE.

sichuan.name: Ba-Shu
sichuan.summary: Ancient kingdoms of Ba and Shu in what is now Sichuan province, southwestern China, absorbed by the Qin around 316 BCE.

dongting-lake.name: Dongting Lake
dongting-lake.summary: A large, shallow lake in Hunan Province, China, that gives Hubei and Hunan their names and is traditionally seen as the birthplace of dragon boat racing.

champa.name: Champa
champa.summary: A collection of Cham polities along the coast of central and southern Vietnam from about the 2nd century CE until 1832, shaped from the 4th century onward by Hinduism.

adze.name: Adze
adze.summary: Ancient cutting tool similar to an axe but with its blade set perpendicular to the handle, used since the Stone Age for shaping wood.

maritime-southeast-asia.name: Maritime Southeast Asia
maritime-southeast-asia.summary: Region comprising Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Timor-Leste, also called Island or Insular Southeast Asia, known for its many islands and rich biodiversity.

a-b-t-culture.name: Đa Bút culture
a-b-t-culture.summary: An early Neolithic period and site in Vietnam dated to about 5000 to 1000 BCE, excavated in the 1930s by Étienne Patte, showing evidence of hunting, fishing and early farming.

hoabinhian.name: Hoabinhian
hoabinhian.summary: A stone-tool tradition linked to hunter-gatherer societies across Southeast Asia, dated from roughly 10,000 to 2000 BCE.

island-melanesia.name: Island Melanesia
island-melanesia.summary: A subregion of Melanesia in Oceania, located east of New Guinea, stretching from the Bismarck Archipelago to New Caledonia.

negrito.name: Negrito
negrito.summary: A term for several distinct, isolated ethnic groups across Southeast Asia and the Andaman Islands, including peoples of the Philippines, Malaysia and Thailand.
